metadata.case_name: LEUNG WING v. CHAN HOI YIN

plaintiff.occupation_before: Transportation worker for his father-in-law; previously skilled carpenter in a boatyard
plaintiff.occupation_after: Welder (various employers including Mass Transit Railway Corporation and Hong Kong Macaw Ferry Wharf)

source: These are described in the Statement of Claim as multiple lacerations over the face, fractures of nasal bone, left zygoma and medial wall and floor of orbit, a 6 cm. haematoma in maxilla, a chronic dacryocystitis of left eye with blockage of the left nasolacrimal duct, and inflammation and tenderness of the left lacrimal sac, and facial assymetry due to enopthalmos on the left side (this means that the left eye is sunken in its socket).
The Plaintiff was admitted to hospital and his lacerations were sutured and an open reduction of the fractured zygoma was carried out by a dental unit of Queen Mary Hospital.

These are described in the Statement of Claim as multiple lacerations over the face, fractures of nasal bone, left zygoma and medial wall and floor of orbit, a 6 cm. haematoma in maxilla, a chronic dacryocystitis of left eye with blockage of the left nasolacrimal duct, and inflammation and tenderness of the left lacrimal sac, and facial assymetry due to enopthalmos on the left side (this means that the left eye is sunken in its socket).
The damage to the bones of the face leading to the deformity of the left eye socket cannot now be corrected.

source: These are described in the Statement of Claim as multiple lacerations over the face, fractures of nasal bone, left zygoma and medial wall and floor of orbit, a 6 cm. haematoma in maxilla, a chronic dacryocystitis of left eye with blockage of the left nasolacrimal duct, and inflammation and tenderness of the left lacrimal sac, and facial assymetry due to enopthalmos on the left side (this means that the left eye is sunken in its socket).
The Plaintiff was admitted to hospital and his lacerations were sutured and an open reduction of the fractured zygoma was carried out by a dental unit of Queen Mary Hospital.
Unfortunately this was not immediately successful and because of the fracture, a further operation was required to wire the zygoma which was again done by the oral surgeons.
The damage to the bones of the face leading to the deformity of the left eye socket cannot now be corrected.

injuries.description: chronic dacryocystitis of left eye with blockage of the left nasolacrimal duct (resulting in constantly watering left eye)
source: These are described in the Statement of Claim as multiple lacerations over the face, fractures of nasal bone, left zygoma and medial wall and floor of orbit, a 6 cm. haematoma in maxilla, a chronic dacryocystitis of left eye with blockage of the left nasolacrimal duct, and inflammation and tenderness of the left lacrimal sac, and facial assymetry due to enopthalmos on the left side (this means that the left eye is sunken in its socket).

Dr. Heffernan in his report dated 28th May 1984 gives as his opinion that the problem of the watering left eye can be partly corrected by surgery as it is caused by blockage to the nasolacrimal tear duct but the problem with the eye-lids cannot now be put right and so the Plaintiff will be left with a permanent problem of watering to some extent.

With regard to the present complaints ... severe watering of his left eye particularly when he gets hot, which causes blurring of his eye sight while working, he has to constantly clean his eye to reduce the blurring, although he states that the vision of his left eye is always blurred and not just when watering.

injuries.description: loss of sensation in the region of the left upper teeth, the skin of the left upper lip and the skin over cheek along the left side of the nose (due to nerve damage)
injuries.body_part: left upper gums, left upper lip, left cheek
source: Apart from the very obvious facial assymetry and sunken left eye socket caused by the fracture to the facial bones Mr. Leung has been left with a number of continuing disabilities, which include a constantly watering left eye with occasional yellow discharge, double vision on looking to the right blurred vision in his left eye, and a loss of sensation in the region of the left upper teeth, the skin of the left upper lip and tae skin over cheek along the left side of the nose.
The loss of sensation over the left upper gum and cheek of the left side of the nose, Dr. Heffernan says is due to nerve damage for which there is no effective treatment.

injuries.description: inability to close his eye-lids of his left eye as the upper and lower eye-lids no longer meet satisfactorily
source: In addition, the facial assymetry has resulted in an inability on the part of the Plaintiff to close his eye-lids of his left eye as the upper and lower eye-lids no longer meet satisfactorily.

Dr. Heffernan in his report dated 28th May 1984 gives as his opinion that the problem of the watering left eye can be partly corrected by surgery as it is caused by blockage to the nasolacrimal tear duct but the problem with the eye-lids cannot now be put right and so the Plaintiff will be left with a permanent problem of watering to some extent.

injuries.description: diplopia (double vision) caused by damage to the muscle of the left orbit
source: Apart from the very obvious facial assymetry and sunken left eye socket caused by the fracture to the facial bones Mr. Leung has been left with a number of continuing disabilities, which include a constantly watering left eye with occasional yellow discharge, double vision on looking to the right blurred vision in his left eye, and a loss of sensation in the region of the left upper teeth, the skin of the left upper lip and tae skin over cheek along the left side of the nose.
Likewise the diplopia (double vision) caused by the damage to the muscle of the left orbit would now be difficult to correct surgically.

injuries.description: visual loss over his left eye (reported in Dr. Y. T. Hung's report as 'around 73% visual loss over his left eye')
source: I should also mention a report by Dr. Y. T. Hung dated 19th January 1985 written following an examination of the Plaintiff at Yau Ma Tei Ophthalmic Centre, in which he states: "As far as his visual acuity and binocular function is concerned, patient has suffered around 73% visual loss over his left eye".

I am not convinced that this means an actual loss of vision to that extent which would apparently leave him partially blind in the left eye, particularly in view of Dr. Heffernan's report of 28th May 1984 in which on testing the eye-sight, he clearly comes to the conclusion that with unaided vision, the left eye is far weaker than the right which is normal, with corrective lenses the left eye was normal.

losses.description: Facial assymetry and sunken left eye (enopthalmos) causing an obvious and permanent disfigurement with which he will have to live the rest of his life.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: No longer swims because of the discomfort he experiences with water entering his eye.
Disadvantage on the labour market and reduced working efficiency (slower working speed) attributable to his injuries leading to dismissal in September 1984 and future disadvantage in obtaining work.
